    def alienOrder(self, words: List[str]) -> str:

alien-dictionary.content:
An alien language uses lowercase English letters in an unknown order. You are given words, a list that is claimed to be sorted lexicographically by that language's rules.

Return a string containing every distinct letter that appears in words, ordered consistently with the alien alphabet. If no valid order exists (the list contradicts itself, or a word comes before its own prefix), return "". If several orders are valid, return any of them.

Example 1:

Input: words = ["wrt","wrf","er","ett","rftt"]
Output: "wertf"

Example 2:

Input: words = ["z","x"]
Output: "zx"

Example 3:

Input: words = ["z","x","z"]
Output: ""
Explanation: "z" cannot come both before and after "x".

Example 4:

Input: words = ["abc","ab"]
Output: ""
Explanation: A word cannot come before its own prefix.

Constraints:

  • 1 <= words.length <= 1000
  • 1 <= words[i].length <= 100
  • words[i] consists of lowercase English letters
alien-dictionary.title: Alien Dictionary

encode-and-decode-strings.content:
Design a scheme that turns a list of strings into a single string and back again. Implement encode(strs), which returns one string, and decode(s), which returns the original list exactly.

Strings may contain any printable ASCII character, including delimiters you might be tempted to use such as #, , or :. decode runs on a fresh object, so it cannot rely on anything encode stored.

Example 1:

Input: strs = ["neet","code","love","you"]
Output: ["neet","code","love","you"]

Example 2:

Input: strs = ["we","say",":","yes"]
Output: ["we","say",":","yes"]

Example 3:

Input: strs = ["", "#4", ""]
Output: ["","#4",""]
Explanation: Empty strings and strings that look like your format must survive the round trip.

Constraints:

  • 0 <= strs.length < 200
  • 0 <= strs[i].length < 200
  • strs[i] contains printable ASCII characters
encode-and-decode-strings.title: Encode and Decode Strings

graph-valid-tree.content:
You are given n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1 and a list of undirected edges, where edges[i] = [a, b] connects a and b.

Return true if these edges form a valid tree: every node is reachable from every other node and there are no cycles. Otherwise return false.

Example 1:

Input: n = 5, edges = [[0,1],[0,2],[0,3],[1,4]]
Output: true

Example 2:

Input: n = 5, edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[2,3],[1,3],[1,4]]
Output: false
Explanation: Nodes 1, 2 and 3 form a cycle.

Example 3:

Input: n = 4, edges = [[0,1],[2,3]]
Output: false
Explanation: The graph has two separate pieces.

Constraints:

  • 1 <= n <= 2000
  • 0 <= edges.length <= 5000
  • edges[i].length == 2
  • 0 <= a, b < n
  • a != b
  • No edge appears twice
graph-valid-tree.title: Graph Valid Tree

meeting-rooms.content:
Given a list of meeting time intervals where intervals[i] = [start, end], determine whether one person could attend every meeting.

A meeting that ends at time t does not conflict with one that starts at t.

Example 1:

Input: intervals = [[0,30],[5,10],[15,20]]
Output: false

Example 2:

Input: intervals = [[7,10],[2,4]]
Output: true

Example 3:

Input: intervals = [[1,5],[5,10]]
Output: true
Explanation: Back-to-back meetings are fine.

Constraints:

  • 0 <= intervals.length <= 10^4
  • intervals[i].length == 2
  • 0 <= start < end <= 10^6
meeting-rooms.title: Meeting Rooms

number-of-connected-components-in-an-und.content:
There are n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1 and a list of undirected edges, where edges[i] = [a, b].

Return the number of connected components: groups of nodes that can reach each other, with no edge leading outside the group.

Example 1:

Input: n = 5, edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[3,4]]
Output: 2
Explanation: {0, 1, 2} and {3, 4}.

Example 2:

Input: n = 5, edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[2,3],[3,4]]
Output: 1

Example 3:

Input: n = 3, edges = []
Output: 3
Explanation: Each node is its own component.

Constraints:

  • 1 <= n <= 2000
  • 0 <= edges.length <= 5000
  • edges[i].length == 2
  • 0 <= a, b < n
  • a != b
  • No edge appears twice
number-of-connected-components-in-an-und.title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph

walls-and-gates.content:
You are given an m x n grid rooms where each cell is one of:

  • -1: a wall or obstacle,
  • 0: a gate,
  • 2147483647 (INF): an empty room.

Fill each empty room in place with the number of steps to its nearest gate, moving up, down, left or right through non-wall cells. Rooms that cannot reach any gate stay INF. The function returns nothing; the judge inspects rooms afterwards.

Example 1:

Input: rooms = [[INF,-1,0,INF],[INF,INF,INF,-1],[INF,-1,INF,-1],[0,-1,INF,INF]]
Output: [[3,-1,0,1],[2,2,1,-1],[1,-1,2,-1],[0,-1,3,4]]

Example 2:

Input: rooms = [[-1]]
Output: [[-1]]

Example 3:

Input: rooms = [[0,INF,INF]]
Output: [[0,1,2]]

Constraints:

  • m == rooms.length
  • n == rooms[i].length
  • 1 <= m, n <= 250
  • rooms[i][j] is -1, 0 or 2147483647
walls-and-gates.title: Walls and Gates
